assertActorManageAccess double-fetch risk resolved: PATCH/DELETE now pass pre-loaded actor, avoiding N+1

Worker claim-and-crash hang RESOLVED: stale DELIVERING attempts (createdAt > 30s ago) are recovered on next worker tick via OR query. At-least-once delivery: duplicate events possible after crash recovery.

Schedule runner stale recovery RESOLVED: orphaned schedules (nextRunAt=sentinel) are recovered on next scheduler tick via recoverStaleSchedules() with 30s grace threshold. At-least-once semantics: duplicate dispatch possible after crash recovery.

Webhook retry scheduler uses setInterval — no backpressure handling; if a tick takes longer than interval, overlapping ticks may compete for the same attempts (safe due to DB-level claims, but potentially wasteful).

Run executor is child-process isolated via child_process.fork() — each run executes in a separate Node.js process with timeout (5min), crash, and error handling. This provides process-level isolation suitable for MVP. True sandboxing (Docker, cgroups, seccomp) remains a future production upgrade.

Run executor integration test gap — full end-to-end flow (claim → execute → dataset write → log persist → finalize) requires a running PostgreSQL instance. 10 unit tests cover the logic via mocked Prisma.
Dataset item POST ownership gate cannot be tested at HTTP level without a running PostgreSQL instance

Actor lifecycle migration risk: existing actors (zero on MVP DB) will get DRAFT status after prisma migrate. No production data affected yet, but migration path must be handled before production deployment.
Schedule scheduler uses same setInterval pattern as webhook scheduler — no backpressure handling for overlapping ticks, but DB-level claims prevent duplicate dispatch

Platform events are fire-and-forget (void emitEvent) — DB insert failures produce unhandled promise rejections with no retry or logging. 12 unhandled rejection warnings observed in test run from schedule-runner and run-executor tests where emitEvent hits mocked Prisma without platformEvent.create.
PlatformEvent cursor pagination orders by createdAt desc but uses id (cuid) as cursor — stable only because cuids embed timestamps. Ordering between events with identical createdAt is unspecified.
GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/events types filter is case-sensitive against the EventType Prisma enum — mismatched casing silently returns zero results.
No Prisma migration generated for PlatformEvent model — schema exists in prisma/schema.prisma but cannot be applied to a database without running prisma migrate dev.
Lifecycle hook emitEvent calls are not asserted in existing run/schedule/actor tests — fire-and-forget side effects are not verified by the test suite.
